create.name: London Insight Meditation
create.bio:
London Insight Meditation is a small independent charity that brings insight (vipassana) meditation and early Buddhist teaching to London. It began in 1995, when two practitioners travelling back from Gaia House saw that busy Londoners needed teaching closer to home; Christina Feldman put them in touch with Yanai Postelnik, and the early days of 'London Retreats', as it was first called, also drew teachers such as Christopher Titmuss and Stephen and Martine Batchelor. It is now run by volunteer coordinators and trustees with a part-time manager.

The charity has no building of its own. It hires venues in London for day retreats and workshops and runs further courses online, led by a rotating group of experienced insight teachers, many connected with Gaia House, while keeping friendly links with Amaravati and Satipanya. Ritual plays little part; the emphasis is on presenting the teachings plainly for Western practitioners without thinning them out. Events are priced on a sponsor, standard and supported scale and the teachers are supported through dana. A free twice-monthly Dharma Circle meets on Zoom, and recorded talks and guided meditations are shared on Dharma Seed and YouTube.

courses.title: In-person: This Precious Human Life – Contemplating Our Mortality
courses.description: A day retreat in north-west London with Yanai Postelnik on the Buddhist practice of reflecting on death as a way of seeing what matters. Teaching and guided exercises alternate with silent meditation; some experience of silent practice is expected.

courses.title: In-person: A Cool Head, A Warm Heart
courses.description: Christina Feldman leads a day on equanimity warmed by kindness, joy and compassion, as a way of meeting an unsettled world. The day mixes practice periods, teaching and time for questions.

courses.title: Online: The Six Sense Bases – Clarity and Wisdom
courses.description: A two-afternoon online course with Leigh Brasington on a less familiar part of the Buddha's teaching: the five physical senses and the mind as the ground of attachment and of insight, explored through several suttas.

free_resources.title: LIM Dharma Circle
free_resources.description: A free Zoom drop-in twice a month on Monday evenings, hosted by James Blake or one of the charity's community dharma leaders, combining sitting practice with shared reflection on a theme. Just log on; there is nothing to book.

free_resources.title: Video
free_resources.description: LIM's page for its YouTube library of recorded talks and guided meditations by its visiting teachers, free to watch.

Domain confirmed from the link on lim.dharmaseed.org; Crawl-delay: 10 respected on londoninsight.org.
No centre building: day events are held at hired venues (currently King Alfred School, North End Road, NW11); base is London.

Hub links from its Our Teachers page: Jill Shepherd, Ajahn Canda (listed as Venerable Canda), Bernat Font, Bhante Bodhidhamma, Kaira Jewel Lingo, Martin Aylward and Mimi Kuo-Deemer. James Baraz (in the lead) is not named on its site, so not linked; Stephen Batchelor is named only in its early history.
The 14 Nov day retreat on mortality uses death-the-afterlife as a subject; it is a contemplative practice day, not grief therapy.
